title: 🌏 Auckland Asian Networking Night
description:
Looking to meet new people, expand your professional network, or simply enjoy meaningful conversations over a drink?

Auckland Asian Networking Night is a relaxed community meetup inspired by Auckland's diverse Asian community, bringing together people from all backgrounds to connect, share experiences, and build genuine relationships.

You don't have to be Asian to join. If you enjoy meeting people from diverse backgrounds and appreciate Asian cultures, you're more than welcome.

No presentations. No formal agenda. Just good conversations.

👥 WHO'S THIS FOR?
Whether you're:

* A professional from any industry
* An entrepreneur or small business owner
* A freelancer or creative
* A student or working holiday maker
* Looking for a new career opportunity
* Or simply interested in meeting new people

💬 WHAT TO EXPECT
Grab a drink, introduce yourself, and join any conversation that interests you.

There's no fixed seating, no scheduled activities, and no pressure. Simply move around, meet different people, and enjoy conversations at your own pace.

You might leave with:

* New friends
* Professional connections
* Career insights
* Business opportunities
* Collaboration ideas
* Or simply a great evening with interesting people

Most people attend on their own, so don't worry if you're coming solo. We'll help you feel welcome.

📍 EVENT DETAILS

* Location: Mixed 1981 Cafe, 50 Fort St, Auckland CBD, Auckland
* Time: 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM (feel free to arrive a little earlier to grab a drink)
* Frequency: Every two weeks
* Capacity: Limited spaces available
* Entry: FREE for Hanahub members (Free to sign up at [hanahub.co.nz](https://www.hanahub.co.nz/))

☕ This event is proudly sponsored by Mixed 1981. All attendees are required to purchase at least one drink, and Hanahub members can enjoy 15% OFF food and drinks by showing their Hanahub member profile on the night.

🍪 Korean snacks will be served on the night, so come and enjoy a taste of Korea while you mingle.

title: EMC English Conversation Club
description:
**EMC English Conversation Club**
**Thursdays, 4 to 6pm**
**Free.** Please **join this group** and **reserve** your seat every week.

Whether you want to improve your English or you're a native speaker keen to help others, this is a great place to connect and build friendships.
This is not a classroom. It’s a relaxed community space where you can share stories, practise everyday English, and learn about life, work, and culture in New Zealand and other countries.
Each session is guided by an experienced facilitator and supported by friendly volunteers.
**What to expect:**
• Casual, friendly conversations on real-life topics
• Supportive facilitators and volunteers
• Language learning through connection, not pressure
• A welcoming environment to build friendships and confidence

Please **join this group** and **reserve** your seat every week.

title: From Vibe Coding to Production AI on AWS
location: Level 19, Vero Centre, 48 Shortland Street, Auckland CBD, Auckland
description:
Hello everyone,

Welcome to the September edition of the Auckland AWS Tools & Programming Meetup! This month, we are diving deep into the lifecycle of building and scaling AI-powered products—from a single idea and "vibe coding" all the way to robust engineering practices for production systems on AWS.

🚨 **Action Required:** To help us streamline building security and sort out the catering (including dietary requirements), please make sure to pre-register before arriving: 👉 **[Pre-register for Venue Check-In Here](https://eventspaces.app/e/auckland-aws-tools-and-programming-meetup-sept-24-from-vibe-coding-to-production-ai-on-aws-a9b5de/register)**

Join us for an exciting double-header exploring the realities of shipping real software:

**Speaker 1: Dinesh Sharma**
**From Zero to Qazo: Building a Product with Kiro, AI & AWS**

**About the Talk:** "I started Qazo with a simple idea and used Kiro and AI to turn it into a real product, eventually deploying it on AWS. This session is about that journey — what worked, what didn't, the lessons I learned from vibe coding, and why I think everyone should try building something of their own to experience the full journey from idea → build → break → learn → deploy."
🔗 **Check out Qazo:** [https://qazo.net](https://qazo.net)

**Speaker 2: Dinesh Liyanage**

**After the Demo: From Vibe Coding to AI Engineering**

* **Evals** so prompt changes stop being guesswork.
* **Tracing** so you can reproduce the bad output a customer reported.
* **Cost and model routing** so unit economics survive growth.
* **Context engineering** so quality doesn't quietly rot as you add data.

title: When I Saw You (Jordan 2012) 1.30 mins
description:
We are in a season of films on Sunday afternoon about films about life in a war zone, especially Palestine.
I have chosen films that are not propaganda.
The attempt is to lift ourselves above that and do a deep dive into the realities of life in such areas. In this film, Tarek and his mother, Ghaydaa, cross the border from Palestine to Jordan along with tens of thousands of other people.

**When I Saw You** was selected at as the Palestinian entry for the best foreign language film at the Academy Awards. The New York Times reviewer wrote:
"A soft-centered child's-eye view of alienation, toughened by fine acting and Hlne Louvart's full-bodied photography."

The Total Film reviewer wrote: "political without point-scoring, Jacir remains true to a child's-eye view, with Asfa's delightful, exuberant performance always upfront."

"Palestinian filmmaker Annemarie Jacir's second film is slight yet significant - and, because of the situation in Syria, timely - story about a boy whose courage inspires hope among the hopeless."

A must-see for us all as we a look into the lives of familes fleeing from war - anywhere.
